name: global_retfound_sae
title: Sparse decomposition of global RETFound embeddings
hypothesis: Global sparse features associate with DR grades and image-level lesion presence.
related_work_gap: Retinal foundation-model representations remain under-explored, but LanSE already establishes medical sparse encoders on chest X-rays.
minimal_experiment: Train global Top-K SAEs on EyePACS embeddings and test lesion association on DDR/IDRiD.
risk: Low novelty and weak spatial evidence; global resizing may erase small lesions.

name: dual_scale_spatial_sae
title: Dual-scale sparse features with lesion-mask and occlusion validation
hypothesis: Separate global and high-resolution tile SAEs recover stable global context and spatially localized lesion features.
related_work_gap: LanSE demonstrates medical sparse encoders but identifies region/token-level localization as future work; retinal masks allow direct spatial and intervention tests.
minimal_experiment: Train both SAEs without lesion labels, freeze them, then evaluate predefined DR lesions on DDR development and locked IDRiD/FGADR external sets.
risk: Large tile compute, small external mask sets, scale and optic-disc confounding.

name: lesion_transcoder
title: Task-targeted sparse transcoders for rare retinal lesions
hypothesis: A supervised lesion transcoder improves rare-lesion feature coverage over reconstruction-only SAEs.
related_work_gap: LanSE uses transcoders for rare targeted patterns, so a retinal adaptation alone is not sufficiently novel.
minimal_experiment: Train a lesion classifier on DDR development data and sparsely transcode its hidden activations.
risk: Supervision weakens unsupervised-discovery claims and can overfit limited masks.
